bullets: Conversations capture something essays cannot — the way dialogue actually unfolds in real time — and the second-order effect of that difference is what most people miss.
The texture of dialogue is the work rather than a byproduct of it; ignoring that means rebuilding it from scratch a year later.
Long-form is not a length but a posture — internalizing that distinction makes the rest of the decisions easier, a pattern observed at teams using Substack.
Outside of Patreon-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot, so the framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs are being made.
The trade-offs around long form cross-cut every other theme — dialogue, cultural drift, and platform choice — rather than standing as a separate concern.
Practical adoption favors running one idea for two weeks rather than overhauling everything at once; the rest is iteration.
